properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured, one pair unseparated): in the dev_reflow2 hub, prior discussion of nested hubs in reflow2's design reached the agent three times (top search hit, a text pointer in flo2, the trial log) and was never opened; a flo2 requirement was written without it and the agent told the owner "wasn't stated anywhere". Search reach refuted; the operative cause is the agent reading a sibling's hits as routing rather than precedent, and nothing in the hub skill, the write guard or an absence claim checks for it
properties.source: dev_reflow2 hub session transcript 2026-09-28; hub skill and capture-intent SKILL.md at the #620 branch; reflow2 committed export's edges
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh) on Anthony's /root-cause, 2026-09-28, dev_reflow2 hub.

① OBSERVED. Capturing Anthony's definition of done for the hub, the agent searched flo2 three times and reflow2 twice, then wrote flo2's req:a-hub-can-be-one-of-another-hubs-designs citing only flo2 nodes ("no requirement said so") and told him in chat, of a hub inside a hub: "Wasn't stated anywhere." Anthony: "we've definitely discussed this prior." Expected: the requirement cites the 2026-09-22 and 09-26 tier brainstorms and their counterpoints (tiers are a graph, not a tree; a level is a position, not a kind). NOT affected: precedent inside flo2, the destination, was found, read and linked, and flo2's own write guard fired and was read.

② PRECEDENT. fact:three-searches-that-did-not-happen-and-what-each-one-cost (08-17: prose assertions about what the graph holds, made without looking); fact:the-brainstorms-only-search-was-the-write-guard-and-it-returned-only-nodes-the-session-had-just-written (09-22); req:a-write-is-warned-when-the-same-thing-already-lives-in-a-related-design (accepted 09-22); dec:idea-a-fact-has-one-home-across-a-family-of-designs-and-reflow2-enforces-it (open). NEW HERE: the search was run and the hit came back.

③⑤ CANDIDATES AND MEASUREMENTS.
C1 search reach / vocabulary — REFUTED. The first reflow2 search ("hub parent design holds children nested tiered hub") returned dec:idea-a-graph-whose-children-are-themselves-reflow2-designs as its TOP hit (27.5), and dec:idea-the-org-ladder-and-the-assembly-ladder-are-read-against-each-other at #11. The same history also reached the agent through flo2's dec:idea-a-person-at-a-higher-tier-reaches-the-designs-below, read in full, which names that reflow2 node in text, and through dev_reflow2's docs/TRIAL-LOG.md section "Late on 09-26: tiered hubs", read in full. Not returned by the agent's queries: dec:idea-a-top-level-graph-holds-what-the-component-graphs-share, dec:nested-graphs (reachable from the top hit).
C2 the instructions scope search to the destination — TEXT CONFIRMED, PREDICTION REFUTED. Hub skill line 63: "Search before you create, in the design you are writing to"; capture-intent's step is single-design. It predicts no reflow2 search; two were run. A weaker form survives: nothing says a sibling's hit is precedent to read and cite rather than a routing signal.
C3 the only mechanical check sees one design — PREMISE CONFIRMED, CAUSATION NOT SHOWN. No capability SATISFIES req:a-write-is-warned-when-the-same-thing-already-lives-in-a-related-design (committed export edges: AUTHORED_BY, EVOLVES_INTO, MITIGATES only). flo2's guard named only flo2 nodes. Three signals already in context were not acted on, so whether a fourth, advisory one would have been is not established.
C4 the agent's framing (outside the tooling) — SUPPORTED. Before writing, eight flo2 nodes were opened and zero reflow2 nodes. The tier history was filed as neighbouring topics (who may reach what; what a parent holds), and "nesting" was scoped to flo2's mechanics. The record's claim was narrow and true; the chat claim was broad and false.
C5 the observation is wrong — REFUTED. The brainstorm text describes hubs over hubs ("a hub over all the individual car types ... each higher level hub is just a client of a set of the next lower hubs"), and no requirement in either design states nesting works.
C2-weak and C4 predict the same observation and cannot be separated without a controlled rerun.

⑥ CLASS. (1) An ABSENCE CLAIM carries no scope: "not stated anywhere" was a check of one design's requirements, generalised; the same class as the 08-17 fact, on the unguarded read path; the brainstorm skill fixed it for itself the same day (reflow2 #615) and no other skill has. (2) Across a family of designs the one-home invariant rests on memory: the hub skill aims search at the destination, the write guard is single-design, and the accepted cross-design warning is unbuilt — the "rule somebody must remember" Anthony objected to on 09-22.

FIXES PROPOSED, NOT APPLIED (awaiting Anthony): build the cross-design warning, pinned by a test that fails today (write into design A what related design B already holds; the reply names B's node); the hub skill searches every design the session reaches and reads and cites a settled or brainstormed hit on the same subject; a standing rule that an absence claim names where it was checked.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: which of C2-weak and C4 operated; whether C3's warning would have changed the outcome; the agent's categorisation is read from its own transcript, not measured independently.

═══ ADDED 2026-09-29 — A SECOND OCCURRENCE, ON THE ROOT-CAUSE PATH, AND THIS TIME THE SIBLING WAS NEVER SEARCHED ═══
dev_reflow2 hub, root-causing flo2.io's "tools fetch failed" for a design added to the hub (recorded in flo2's design as the root cause of a forgotten engine session recovered on tool calls only, 2026-09-28). Step ② (the raw-error search) was run in flo2's design only — twice, on the verbatim error texts — because flo2 was the design being worked. reflow2's design already held fact:root-cause-an-idle-session-expires-and-the-proxy-silently-takes-a-new-seat-so-live-claims-read-gone (2026-09-23): the 300 s rmcp session keep-alive, the same "Session not found" 404, and a ⑨ naming flo2's gateway as the unmeasured case. MEASURED afterwards: the same raw-error query in reflow2's design returns it as hit #3.
COST: the fix was right (it recovers any forgotten session), but flo2's finding named the wrong trigger (the 15-minute design idle close, v0.73.0) and left the engine's "0 session(s) ended" unexplained until a later read of drain.rs end_sessions showed the count is the session table's size at close — already empty, because sessions expire at 5 minutes.
WHAT IT ADDS TO THE CLASS: here C2 held in its STRONG form — the search was aimed only at the design being worked, although the failing part (flo2's gateway) sits on reflow2's seam and reflow2's design owns the mechanism. The 09-28 case was a sibling hit returned and not read; this is a sibling never asked. Both leave the one-home invariant resting on the agent's framing. Found while running capture-session, not by the root-cause pass itself.
